title: The SPAC Sponsor Behind Lucid and Oklo Is Taking Agility Robotics Public on Nov. 5. Here's What Those 2 Stocks Did in Their First 90 Days.

The SPAC Sponsor Behind Lucid and Oklo Is Taking Agility Robotics Public on Nov. 5. Here's What Those 2 Stocks Did in Their First 90 Days.
Leo Sun, The Motley Fool

CCXI
NVDA

AMZN

Trading disclosure

Agility Robotics, a developer of humanoid robots for warehouses, logistics hubs, and manufacturing plants, will go public through a merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI (NASDAQ: CCXI), a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC), on Nov. 4. Its stock will start trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "AGLT" on Nov. 5.

Agility's flagship product is Digit, a bipedal humanoid robot that can move heavy items and navigate narrow aisles, stairs, and ramps on its own. Nvidia and Amazon back it, and it's signed multi-year contracts with Toyota, GXO Logistics, MercadoLibre, and Schaffer.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Agility Robotics.

Agility generated only $1.8 million in revenue in 2025, yet it has a backlog of over $300 million. It's going public to raise the capital to convert that backlog into revenue. It believes it can deploy its first Digit v5 units by the end of 2026, and to eventually deploy 800 units in 2027, 7,000 units in 2030, and up to 25,000 units in 2035 as it scales its business.

That's an ambitious outlook, but many SPAC-backed companies tend to overpromise and underdeliver. To see where Agility's stock might be headed, let's see what happened to two other companies that went public through mergers with Churchill Capital's SPACs -- Lucid (NASDAQ: LCID) and Oklo (NYSE: OKLO) -- in their first 90 days of public trading.

What happened to Lucid?

Lucid, a developer of high-end electric vehicles, initially attracted significant attention because it was led by Peter Rawlinson, Tesla's former chief vehicle engineer. It launched its first vehicle, the Air sedan, in 2021 and its second, the Gravity SUV, in 2024.

Lucid closed its merger with Churchill Capital IV on July 24, 2021, and began trading at a reverse-split-adjusted price of $252.40 per share on July 26. It closed at $369.90 per share 90 days later. But as of this writing, it trades at about $3.50.

Lucid's stock plummeted because it completely missed its original targets. Before going public, Lucid claimed its annual vehicle deliveries would reach 20,000 in 2022, 49,000 in 2023, 90,000 in 2024, and 135,000 in 2025. In reality, it only delivered 4,369 vehicles in 2022, 6,001 in 2023, 10,241 in 2024, and 15,841 in 2025. It blamed its sluggish expansion on supply chain constraints, the Gravity's delayed launch, macro headwinds, and intense competition.

Key Takeaways

MercadoLibre reports third-quarter results after the close on Nov. 4, and analysts expect revenue to grow about 44% but EPS only 13%.

The bull case depends on profit growth coming back, with consensus calling for normalized EPS to jump 46% in 2027 after a small dip this year.

The operating margin fell to 6.7% in the second quarter from 12.2% a year earlier, and management has said it doesn't expect that level to change much in the near term.

The report has to show the margin has stopped falling, because investors paying 41x forward earnings are already paying for much of the 2027 rebound.

MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) reports third-quarter results after the close today, Wednesday, Nov. 4. Its bulls need one thing from the report: proof that all that sales growth is turning back into profit.

The stock fell 10% in the week after Lula's surprise win in Brazil's Oct. 25 runoff. With the election settled, investors are left with one question: can earnings grow fast enough to carry the stock?

The bull case is a 2027 story

Analysts expect normalized EPS to slip to $38.26 this year from $39.40 in 2025. After that they expect it to jump to $55.89 in 2027 and $78.56 in 2028, nearly double last year's figure:

MercadoLibre (MELI): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

Analysts have been moving the other way, though. Between September 2025 and October 2026, they cut their 2026 EPS estimate by 42% while raising their 2026 revenue estimate by 17%. MercadoLibre has delivered the sales analysts hoped for, and less of the profit.

TIKR tracks 26 analysts on MercadoLibre. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on MercadoLibre, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See MercadoLibre's Analyst Ratings

The margin is still sliding

The bull case needs the operating margin to turn. Instead, it has fallen by more than half since mid-2024, from 14.3% to 6.7%:

MercadoLibre (MELI): operating (EBIT) margin (%), last 12 quarters (to June 30, 2026) (TIKR)

Second-quarter revenue rose 50% to $10.2 billion, the fastest growth in four years, while operating income fell 17% to $683 million. Across MercadoLibre's four country segments, profit before corporate costs was $2,948 million in the first half of 2026. A year earlier it was $2,950 million, on 49% less revenue.

All that extra scale went straight back into the business.

Most of the spending has gone into three things:

Free shipping in Brazil, where MercadoLibre lowered its free-shipping threshold to R$19 from R$79 in June 2025.

The Mercado Pago credit card, which still lost money after funding costs and loan losses in the second quarter.

Keeping Amazon and Shopee from taking market share.

title: Down 38%, Is MercadoLibre Stock a Better Buy than SpaceX and the "Magnificent Seven" Stocks in November?
detail:
Down 38%, Is MercadoLibre Stock a Better Buy than SpaceX and the "Magnificent Seven" Stocks in November?
Jennifer Saibil, The Motley Fool

The "Magnificent Seven" stocks, which include Nvidia, Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta Platforms, and Tesla, offer a certain stability to investors. They are already among the most valuable companies in the world, but they continue to demonstrate growth and potential, which is why the market loves them.

Space Exploration Technologies is not part of the group, although it fits right into the megacap category. Since it's fairly young, and it has the latest technology, the market expects a lot from it. That's why it's worth $1.8 trillion.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

But there are plenty of smaller stocks that can offer a lot more to investors. Because they still have so much room to grow, over time, they may perform much better than the megacap stocks.

Consider MercadoLibre (NASDAQ: MELI). It recently was 38% off its highs, but it has incredible opportunities. Here's why it could be the better stock to buy in November.

The fabulous performance

MercadoLibre is growing faster than all of the Magnificent Seven. It's not growing as fast as SpaceX, but MercadoLibre is a lot cheaper, which is why it has more room to grow.

Image source: Getty Images.

In the second quarter, revenue increased 50% year over year, its fastest rate in almost four years. That's on a higher base and during a challenging time for the economy, with high inflation in many of the 18 countries it serves.

Gross merchandise volume increased 44% year over year, and MercadoLibre ships 78% of shipments (besides the ones customers choose to be slow) within 48 hours. Unique active buyers increased 26%.

Total payment volume increased 56% year over year. Assets under management were up 68%, and monthly active users were up 30%.

The enticing opportunity

Latin America lags behind other global regions in both e-commerce penetration and digital finance, giving MercadoLibre years of growth potential. And the company sees its ecosystem as its path toward reaching it.

Management says that the dual commerce and finance platform "creates a flywheel in which each makes the other stronger, and why deepening engagement is what accelerates that flywheel into a durable competitive advantage."

It measures this flywheel in engagement, which you can see in many of its metrics. Items per buy increased 14% year over year in Q2, and the ratio of daily active buyers to monthly active buyers reached its highest level ever, for example.

MercadoLibre is heading into its November 4 third quarter report after heavy spending on Brazilian logistics and credit expansion, with management reiterating that Brazil's credit trends remain stable despite recent political shifts.

The firm has intentionally accepted lower operating margins through fee cuts and free shipping in Brazil. Citi's upgrade highlights how these reinvestment choices and credit quality signals are reshaping external expectations for the business.

We will now explore how MercadoLibre's investment narrative could be influenced by Brazil focused reinvestment and the upcoming earnings release.

Scan how MercadoLibre's earnings setup compares with other heavily reinvesting platforms by reviewing the hand picked 34 high quality undervalued stocks that pair reinvestment with balance sheet strength.

MercadoLibre Investment Narrative Recap

To own MercadoLibre, you need to be comfortable with a business that is trading some profitability today for ecosystem depth in Brazil, especially in logistics and credit. Management is leaning into free shipping, fee cuts and longer duration loans. The key short term catalyst is the November 4 earnings report, where investors will focus on how these choices show up in operating margin and credit metrics.

That 10% share price drop after Brazil's election adds noise but does not change the core question. The biggest risk remains that Brazil focused credit growth and higher leverage combine with any weakening in repayment behavior or legal scrutiny, which could lift funding costs and keep margins under pressure.

The most relevant recent corporate signal is commentary from MercadoLibre's fintech chief that there is no current deceleration or deterioration in Brazil's credit trends despite political shifts and a weaker real. With Brazil providing a little over half of 2025 revenue, that datapoint matters directly to the credit expansion narrative.

Investors watching the November 4 release are effectively testing that statement against fresh data. Asset quality, provisioning and non performing loan ratios will sit alongside logistics efficiency and shipping cost per unit as key proof points. Citi's recent upgrade frames sentiment, but the real driver from here is how consistently MercadoLibre executes on the Brazil credit and logistics playbook.

MercadoLibre's current analyst narrative points to revenues of US$75.8b and earnings of US$5.2b by 2029, based on assumed yearly revenue growth of 29.1% and an increase in earnings of about US$3.3b from US$1.9b today.

Key Takeaways

Nu Holdings stock fell 14% in a month after President Lula unexpectedly won Brazil's Oct. 25 presidential runoff.

MercadoLibre and other US-listed Brazilian stocks fell with it.

Nu's quarterly profit topped $1 billion for the first time in the second quarter.

For investors who can live with Brazil's political swings, the drop looks like a chance to load up.

Nu Holdings (NU:NYSE) stock is down 14% in the past month, and Brazil's voters did most of the damage.

Investors had bet on Flávio Bolsonaro after his surprise first-round showing. Then President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won the Oct. 25 runoff, and Nu sold off along with MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) and the rest of Brazil's US-listed stocks.

MercadoLibre said its second-quarter revenue grew 50% to $10.2 billion, with Brazil showing the strongest trends. Its report this week covers a quarter that ended before the vote, so what management has seen in Brazil since then matters more than the numbers.

Nu's own news was quieter. On Oct. 23, it said CTO Eric Young is leaving, and CEO David Vélez is overseeing technology until it finds a replacement. Nu says its priorities haven't changed, and its numbers haven't either.

TIKR tracks 23 analysts on Nu Holdings. How many say "Buy"?

Nu's quarterly profit passed $1 billion

In the second quarter, net income passed $1 billion for the first time, revenue grew 39%, and return on equity hit 33%. On Invest Like the Best on Oct. 13, Vélez said that against the big incumbent banks, "we end up with a return on equity that is 2 to 3x their return on equity."

Loans more than 90 days overdue rose to 6.9% of the book in the second quarter. Management put that mostly down to seasonality, and Nu is also choosing to lend to riskier borrowers.

Analysts expect normalized EPS to more than double from 2025 to 2028.

The cheapest it's been in three years

At Monday's close, Nu traded at 4.6x tangible book value, against an 8.3x average over the past three years.

The $18.80 consensus target sits 62% above Monday's close.

Nu Holdings (NU): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)
Load up, if you can stomach Brazil

Investors are pricing Nu as if Lula's win breaks its business, and nothing Nu has reported says it does. With earnings growing and the stock at the bottom of its three-year valuation range, I'd buy, as long as Brazil's swings won't shake you out.

MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) will report third-quarter earnings on Wednesday at a trying time for the stock.

Shares sold off sharply last week as part of a broader rout in Brazilian stocks after Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won reelection as Brazil's president, contradicting expectations. MercadoLibre is now down 16% year-to-date as profits have fallen due to rising competition and investments in the business.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Will MercadoLibre rise or fall after its earnings report Wednesday afternoon? Let's take a look at what to expect.

Image source: MercadoLibre.

What to expect when MercadoLibre reports

MercadoLibre doesn't provide guidance, which tends to make quarterly reports more volatile, so investors should expect significant movement in the stock after the report, as they have less of a gauge to measure the results.

The analyst consensus calls for revenue to grow 44.6% to $10.7 billion and for earnings per share to increase from $8.32 to $9.27, showing that margins are still expected to narrow.

Investors will be closely watching operating margin as the market is wary of the impact of MercadoLibre's investment cycle. The company is investing in logistics operations after lowering its free shipping threshold in order to remain competitive as entrants like Amazon and Sea Limited's Shopee try to gain market share. Additionally, the company is investing in its credit card business, which has weighed on margins, as the expansion entails upfront marketing and onboarding costs, as well as an accounting adjustment for expected future credit losses, even though no revenue has been collected.

In the third quarter, we're likely to hear something similar about this investment strategy as we did in Q2 when management said its credit book "continues to be very profitable," and added, "It's this overall strength, strong cash generation, robust profitability, and a healthy balance sheet that give us the confidence to keep investing at the pace we are."

Why MercadoLibre stock could jump after the Q3 report

After falling 16% so far this year, there's a good argument that the stock is a bargain. It's recouped some of its losses from the post-election sell-off, but even that decline seemed unreasonable, as the company has done just fine with Lula in charge, putting together an unmatched streak of 30 straight quarters of 30% or better revenue growth.

An emerging-markets manager made three US-listed bets last quarter. Brazil's election, an RBI hike and a bank probe have split them apart since June.

Westwood Global Investments' 13F for the quarter ended June 30, filed August 7, shows a new stake in MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) and bigger ones in Yum China (YUMC:NYSE) and HDFC Bank (HDB). The Boston fund held $2.85 billion of US-listed stocks across 11 positions.

Since quarter-end, Yum China is up 12%, MercadoLibre is down 4%, and HDFC Bank is down 14%. All three still trade 22% to 41% below their 52-week highs. This week matters for two of them: Yum China reports on Tuesday, November 3, and MercadoLibre on Wednesday, November 4. The fund's September-quarter 13F is due by November 16.

MercadoLibre Is Growing Faster and Earning Less

MercadoLibre was the new name: 203,266 shares worth $345 million at June 30. That was 12.1% of the fund's 13F stocks and its third-biggest position. The stock is down 4% from that quarter-end price (a 13F doesn't show what the fund paid).

The second quarter shows the trade-off. Revenue rose 50% to $10.2 billion. Operating income fell 17% to $683 million, and the operating margin shrank to 6.7%, as MercadoLibre kept spending on free shipping and its credit card. Analysts have cut their 2026 EPS estimate 42% since September 2025, from $66.55 to $38.38, and their mean price target has dropped 21%:

MELI Stock Mean Price Target: Oct 2025-Oct 2026 (TIKR)

Then Brazil voted. MercadoLibre stock fell 10% in a week, most of it on October 26, the first trading day after Lula won the runoff. Citi upgraded the stock to Buy after the drop, though it trimmed its target to $2,050 from $2,100.

Even the lowest target, $1,750, sits above the $1,624.53 close. At about 39x forward earnings, the stock trades well below its 48x quarter-end average since 2023. Wednesday's results will show whether that 6.7% margin has stopped sliding.

MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI is strengthening its profitability potential by encouraging customers to engage with both its e-commerce marketplace and Mercado Pago fintech services. These customers, referred to as ecosystemic users, represent an increasingly important part of its business model, as deeper participation across both platforms creates opportunities for greater engagement and stronger customer economics.

Ecosystemic users demonstrate significantly higher shopping activity than marketplace-only customers, purchasing more products across a wider range of categories. Their engagement also extends to financial services, where they generate greater payment volumes, maintain higher assets under management and use more financial products. This interconnected activity strengthens the relationship between commerce and fintech, making customers more valuable to the broader ecosystem.

We also note that profit contribution from ecosystemic users substantially exceeds the combined contribution of customers using the marketplace and fintech services separately. This suggests that integrating shopping and financial services creates economic value beyond what either business could generate independently. Mercado Pago credit cards reinforce this relationship by encouraging customers to remain engaged across both platforms.

The growing adoption of cross-platform services underscores MercadoLibre's ability to deepen customer relationships and strengthen monetization opportunities. Management believes this interconnected ecosystem provides a structural competitive advantage that is difficult to replicate.

How Does MercadoLibre Stack Up Against Its Industry?

MercadoLibre, which competes with Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN and Sea Limited SE, has seen its shares tumble 14.4% over the past three months compared with the industry's 15.7% decline. While Amazon shares have fallen 15.4%, Sea Limited has plunged 33.2% in the aforementioned period.

We're in the thick of earnings season. The market has also been volatile, explaining why so many blue chip stocks were moving aggressively following the release of fresh financials.

This will be a busy slate of quarterly reports this week. Several stocks you know will be announcing their results. Three companies that could shape the way this week plays out are Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), and MercadoLibre (NASDAQ: MELI). Let's take a closer look at these three companies that will be posting their latest numbers through the first three days of this week.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
1. Advanced Micro Devices

After more than doubling this year, AMD stock is the biggest gainer of the three companies I'm profiling this week. The provider of central processing units (CPUs) and graphics processing units (GPUs) has also more than quadrupled over the past five years.

AMD has emerged as a popular play on AI infrastructure. The revolution is happening, and AMD is one of the leaders providing the ammo. Revenue growth is accelerating for the third year in a row, and analysts believe it will pick up the pace again next year.

2023: -4% Revenue growth

2024: 14%

2025: 34%

2026: 47% (est.)

2027: 75% (est.)

The top-line jumps have been substantial and should continue to be. The bottom line is growing even faster.

When AMD reports its fiscal third-quarter results on Tuesday afternoon, analysts expect revenue to rise 42% to $13 billion. This may be a step down from the 50% top-line jump it posted three months ago, but it's still the second-strongest revenue growth it has posted in the last four years.

Analysts see earnings per share soaring 60% in Tuesday's report. It has consistently landed just ahead of Wall Street's quarterly profit targets over the past year.

Some AI stocks are growing faster and delivering wider profit margins. This isn't an AMD defect. It's an opportunity for upside. The valuation is admittedly steep. AMD is trading at 66 times this year's adjusted earnings target and a still-premium multiple of 32 for 2027. With valuations for AI stocks coming under pressure, AMD shares tumbled 17% last month. A strong report can get AMD moving in the right direction again.

2. Apple

Apple's revenue growth is also stepping on the gas. When the consumer tech giant reports fourth-quarter results shortly after Monday's close, it will be Apple's first fiscal year of double-digit growth in five years. With Apple retaking the market cap crown on Friday, all eyes will be on its latest numbers.
